message.content: Research is complete. Let me place the order.
message.reasoning:
Now decide. AAPL at $222.70. Mandate: max $10,000 per order, $20,000 total today, buy only, limit close to market.

$10,000 / 222.70 = 44.9 shares. So 44 shares = $9,798.80. Limit price close to market — say $222.80 or $223.00 (slightly above ask to ensure fill). Let's use $223.00 → 44 × 223 = $9,812, under $10,000.

Key figures: FY2024 revenue $391,035M, net income $93,736M, diluted EPS $6.08, operating income $123,216M. Q4 revenue $94.9B up 6% YoY.

Note: net income declined YoY due to one-time $10.2B tax charge. That's a nuance worth mentioning.

Let me place the order.

Should I include operating_cash_flow? I don't have that figure verified. Only include what I relied on.

Decision: buy 44 shares at limit $223.00.

Actually, let me consider whether to buy at all. The mandate says decide whether to buy. Fundamentals: revenue growth 6% in Q4, FY revenue up 2%, EPS down slightly due to tax charge. Stock at $222.70, near highs. Reasonable to buy a modest position. I'll buy.

Limit price: current ask 222.72. A limit at 223.00 is 0.13% above — close to market. Good.
